_help: The Shipwright's Manual (GuideChapters.java). Each chapter is a button on the left of the book. Lines in 'text': '# ' = heading, '- ' = bullet point, '> ' = tip, '' = empty line, anything else = normal text. Pages are split up by themselves. 'icon' is any item id; Arsenal gear in it is shown made of 'icon_material'. 'color' is a hex colour. 'generated' adds lines written from the mod's own data after the text: materials, traits, weapons, skills, guns, cannons, navy_casting, meito, navy_brass, hunter_gear, upgrades or set_bonuses. 'after' is more text that goes after the generated lines.

chapters.title: Welcome Aboard
text: Every pirate needs a blade they trust. In One Piece Arsenal you don't find your weapons, you build them: every sword, gun and piece of armor is put together from parts, and the material of each part decides how strong it is and what it can do.
# How it works
- Make parts from a material at a crafting table, like a Katana Blade of Ship Iron.
- Carry a full set of parts to a Shipwright's Anvil and forge them into a weapon.
- Each material gives its part a trait. Mix materials to get the traits you want.
- Navy materials and Navy designs have to be taken from the Marines.
# Reading this book
Click a chapter on the left, and use the arrows (or your mouse wheel) to turn pages. The Materials and Traits chapters are written from the mod's own numbers, so they're always up to date.
> Lost this book? Type /arsenalguide for a new one, or craft one from a Book and Driftwood.

chapters.title: Your First Weapon
text: Here's how to forge a Ship Iron katana from scratch.
# 1. Build a Shipwright's Anvil
Put an Anvil on top of any planks in a crafting table.
# 2. Make the parts
A katana needs a Katana Blade, a Tsuba and a Hilt. Make each one from Iron Ingots at a crafting table. Every part has its own shape: open the recipe book and search for the part to see it.
# 3. Forge it
Carry all three parts anywhere in your inventory, then right-click the anvil with an empty hand. The parts don't need to be in a grid. If you carry several sets, the anvil forges them one per click.
# 4. Look it over
Hover over your new katana to see its damage, speed, durability and both its traits. Every forged weapon and armor piece lists what it's made of.
> Driftwood is the cheapest material: two sticks and a kelp make two pieces. Good for practice.

chapters.title: Parts
text: Every piece of gear is made of parts. One part is the head: it does the cutting, shooting or protecting. The others hold it together.
# The head
The blade, axe head, barrel or armor shell. Its material decides the damage (or the armor) and gives the head's blade trait.
# The other parts
Guards, hilts, bindings, handles, firing parts, stocks and linings. Their material decides the speed (or the reload) and gives their handle trait.
# Durability
All the parts share it: the item lasts as long as its parts' durability, averaged.
# Mixing materials

A Kairoseki blade on a Ship Iron hilt hits like Kairoseki, swings like Ship Iron, and has both traits: Seastone from the blade and Riveted from the hilt. That's the whole idea: pick each part for what it gives you.
> Hides and leathers (Sea King Hide, Island Whale Leather) only make armor shells and linings.

chapters.title: Materials
text: Every material, weakest tier first. For comparison, an iron sword does 6 damage and lasts 250 uses, and an armor shell of 4 is as strong as iron armor (5 is diamond).
Blade damage is added to the weapon's own damage, so a katana with a 5-damage blade hits like an iron sword. Handle speed is added to its attack speed.

chapters.title: Traits
text: Each material gives one trait when it's the head and one when it's any other part. Your gear's tooltip lists the traits it has. Traits marked coming soon are planned but don't do anything yet.

chapters.title: Hand Weapons
text: Seven blades and clubs, each built from a head, a binding and a handle (the katana from a blade, tsuba and hilt). Each kind has something only it does.
Pirate and common weapons are forged at a Shipwright's Anvil. Navy designs, and any weapon whose head is a Navy material, need a Marine Armory Bench.
> Katanas, cutlasses and sabres are swords, so the One Piece Mod's whetstones, sword styles, Dials and Haki work on them.

chapters.title: Weapon Skills
text: Every Arsenal hand weapon has a skill of its own. Hold it in your main hand and press X (Options > Controls > Key Binds, under "One Piece Arsenal", to change the key).
# How skills work
- A skill hits for a share of the weapon's own damage, so better parts, grades, levels and upgrades make it stronger. Armament Haki adds 25%.
- Your weapon's material traits go off on skill hits too, like Seastone draining a fruit user.
- Each use costs 1 hunger point and 2 uses of the weapon. You can't use one when you're starving.
- The cooldown shows on the weapon in your hotbar. Every weapon of the same kind shares it.
- Skills that need a target (Iai Draw, Arrest Hook) cost nothing if there's no enemy in reach.
- A graded katana that refuses you won't do its skill either.
> Skills are on their own key, so a katana, cutlass or sabre can still use your fighting style's techniques on Z. Guns have no skill.

chapters.title: Devil Fruit Weapons
text: In One Piece, a few weapons ate a Devil Fruit and came alive: Mr. 4's bazooka Lassoo is a dachshund, and Spandam's sword Funkfreed turns into an elephant. You can do the same.
# Feeding a weapon
- Hold a forged weapon or gun and put a Zoan fruit (an animal fruit) in your offhand, then right-click a Shipwright's Anvil. The weapon eats the fruit.
- Only Zoan fruits can live in a weapon. Paramecia and Logia fruits won't work.
- A weapon only eats one fruit, and anything with a Kairoseki part refuses one: it's the sea turned to stone.
- The fruit's power belongs to the weapon. Anyone can use it, even someone who ate a fruit of their own.
# Waking it up
- Sneak and press the Weapon Skill key (X) with it in your main hand. It turns into its animal and hits with the animal's signature move.
- For 12 seconds it then fights on its own, biting the nearest enemy every second and a half. It goes back to sleep if you put it away.
- Waking it costs 1 hunger point and 4 uses of the weapon, and it can't wake again for a minute after it sleeps.
- Its bites hit for a share of the weapon's own damage, so good parts and upgrades make it stronger. Without Sneak, X still does the weapon's normal skill.

chapters.title: Guns
text: Each gun is built from a barrel, a firing part and a stock. They're One Piece Mod guns, so they take that mod's ammo and its Scopes, Long Barrels, Hair Triggers, Dials, Quick Draw and Sniper's Eye.
# What each part does
- Barrel: the damage, the range, and the blade trait. A Kairoseki barrel drains Devil Fruit users it shoots.
- Firing part: the reload. A light material reloads faster.
- Stock: the aim. A higher tier stock spreads less.

chapters.title: Ship Cannons
text: Out at sea, your ship is only as strong as her guns. A Ship Cannon is a One Piece Mod Cannon you build yourself, and its parts decide how it shoots.
# Forging one

Carry a Cannon Bore, a Fuse and a Gun Carriage to a Shipwright's Anvil and right-click it with an empty hand. The bore and fuse are the same parts the Hand Cannon uses. A Navy bore (like Kairoseki) has to be put together at a Marine Armory Bench.
# What each part does
- Cannon Bore: how hard its cannonballs hit ships and how far they fly.
- Fuse: how fast your crew reloads. A light material reloads faster.
- Gun Carriage: how true it aims. A higher tier carriage spreads less.
A Ship Iron cannon shoots exactly like a plain Cannon. Hover over a cannon to see how it compares.
# Firing it

Place it on deck facing out over the rail, like a plain Cannon. Aboard, press the fire cannons key (M) while looking over that side. On land, right-click it holding a cannonball or shell. When a broadside mixes cannons, the crew reloads as fast as those cannons take on average.
> A ship keeps each cannon's parts while she sails, and a broken cannon drops with its parts still on it.
# Cannon Shells

Shells are cannon ammo made of any material: four from a crafting table (the material around gunpowder, in a plus shape). Navy shells are cast at a Navy station: hold any shell as the pattern, and each one takes one Navy ingot. Hold a stack when you fire and every cannon loads it instead of cannonballs.
- A shell's material sets its hull damage.
- Everyone caught in its burst gets the material's blade trait, as if your gun hit them. Your own crew is safe.
- Kairoseki shells drain every Devil Fruit user aboard the ship they hit. Pacifista Alloy sets her burning, and Vegapunk Compound burns her or freezes her rigging.
> The One Piece Mod's Chain Shot, Fire Shot and Grapeshot still work the same way.

chapters.title: Armor
text: A Hat, Coat, Sash and Boots. Each piece is built from two parts at a Shipwright's Anvil:
- A shell: Hat Crown, Coat Plates, Sash Weave or Boot Soles. Its material sets the defense and gives the blade trait.
- A Lining, of any material, which adds its handle trait.
# Looks

Armor looks like clothes when you wear it, cut by its shell material: Driftwood is a castaway's straw hat and sandals, Ship Iron a pirate captain's tricorn and crimson coat, Marine Standard Steel a recruit's sailor uniform, Kairoseki a Navy officer's coat, Wano Tamahagane and Kokuto a samurai's armor and hakama, Dragon Scale a red scale coat.
# Armor traits
Some traits only matter on armor: Waterproof swims faster, Endurance keeps you from getting hungry, Plated deflects bullets and arrows, and a Kairoseki shell drains Devil Fruit users who hit you.
> Armor shells have a leather pad in the middle of the recipe, so they don't clash with vanilla armor.
> A full set with Navy shells is a Marine uniform. See Marine Disguise.
> Four pieces of the same kind give a set bonus. See Set Bonuses.

chapters.title: Set Bonuses
text: Wear a full set of matching armor (hat, coat, sash and boots) and it does more than each piece alone. A piece's tooltip lists the sets it belongs to.
- Most sets only care about the shells. Linings can be anything, unless the set says otherwise.
- Sets stack: a full Kairoseki set with Navy linings is a Seastone Bulwark and a Regulation Uniform at once.
- Damage cuts from several sets add up, but never take off more than 60% of a hit.
- Marines and famous Navy officers in Arsenal armor get the damage bonuses of their sets too.

chapters.title: Repairs and Upgrades
text: Forged gear isn't finished when it leaves the anvil. Bring it back to mend it, and to fit it with upgrades as you find the materials.
# Mending

Hold the damaged weapon, gun or armor piece and right-click a Shipwright's Anvil. It's mended with the material of its blade, head, barrel or shell, taken from anywhere in your inventory: Iron Ingots for Ship Iron, Seastone Ingots for Kairoseki, and so on. Each piece mends a quarter of it.
> Navy gear can be mended and upgraded at a Shipwright's Anvil too. Only putting it together takes a Marine Armory Bench.
# Upgrading
Hold the gear in your main hand and the upgrade's item in your offhand, then right-click the anvil. Each click adds one level.
- Each kind of gear has a few upgrade slots (listed below). Every level takes a slot, so choose what you want most.
- Each upgrade has a highest level, and only fits some kinds of gear.
- Hover over the gear to see its upgrades and how many slots are left.
> Upgrades stack with the One Piece Mod's whetstones, gun parts, Dials and enchantments, and a katana keeps them when it awakens into a Black Blade.
> If the upgrade's item is also what mends the gear, the offhand wins: empty your offhand to mend it instead.
# Every upgrade

chapters.title: Broken Gear
text: Forged gear doesn't shatter and vanish when it wears out. It stops at its last point of durability and is Broken, and it stays Broken until you do something about it.
# What breaking does
- A broken weapon hits like a bare fist: no damage, traits or upgrades.
- Broken armor stops nothing, and its traits go quiet.
- A broken gun won't fire.
- Its name says Broken, and you hear it go.
# Mending it
Hold it and right-click a Shipwright's Anvil, the same as any worn gear. Each piece of its blade, head, barrel or shell material mends a quarter.
# Taking it apart
Sneak and right-click a Shipwright's Anvil holding forged gear to take it apart for its parts. You can do this to any forged gear, broken or not.
- Gear that still works comes apart into every part.
- Broken gear loses the part that held it together: a katana's tsuba, a weapon's binding or guard, a gun's firing part, or an armor piece's lining. The rest come back.

- The blade, head, barrel or shell remembers the gear it came from. Forge it into the same kind of gear again, with any other parts, and it comes back with its upgrades, whetstone grade, blade level, enchantments, Dials and name.
- Gear that still worked keeps its wear. Broken gear's head comes back unworn, since the snapped part took the wear with it.
> Taking a working katana apart is how you give it a better tsuba or hilt without losing the blade.
> Navy heads still need a Marine Armory Bench to be put back together.

chapters.title: Navy Stations
text: You're a pirate, so the Navy won't sell you its gear. Navy materials have no crafting table recipes, and Navy designs can't be forged at a Shipwright's Anvil. For those you need the Navy's own stations, and the only way to get one is to take it.
# The three stations
- Marine Armory Bench: works like the Shipwright's Anvil, but also puts together Navy gear: the Marine Sabre, the Jitte, and anything whose blade, barrel or shell is a Navy material.
- Quartermaster's Desk and Marine Base Smeltery: right-click with any part as a pattern. You keep it and get a copy made of the station's material, paid for with that material from your inventory.
# Capturing one

Each Marine base has its stations set down inside the first time a player walks in. While any Marine is within 24 blocks the station is guarded: touching it brings the base down on you. An officer's uniform lets you use it without a fight, but not carry it off.
Clear the Marines out, then right-click it to capture it, or mine it and take it home. A captured station gets a Jolly Roger daubed on and works anywhere.
> Keep captured stations out of sight. A Marine who spots one sends a squad after whoever is nearby, and a Marine who reaches it takes it back.
# What each casting station makes

chapters.title: Meito
text: A katana that cuts down enough enemies can become a famous blade. Two gates keep meito rare: the blade has to earn its grade, and you have to be worthy of it.
# Blade levels
Katanas gain levels from kills, more for armed enemies and bosses. Each level adds 0.1 damage. A blade's grade caps its level: 5 ungraded, 10 Skillful, 15 Great, 20 Supreme.
# Raising the grade
Use a One Piece Mod whetstone on it. It only works once the blade is at its level cap, made of a strong enough material, and has done its deed:
- Skillful: a tier 2 or better blade that has cut down 25 armed enemies.
- Great: a tier 3 or better blade that has beaten a named boss.
- Supreme: a tier 3 or better blade that has beaten an Emperor, an Admiral or another top-tier boss.
The katana's tooltip shows how far along it is.
# Worthy wielders

Any graded sword refuses a player who isn't strong enough, the One Piece Mod's famous blades like Wado Ichimonji and Yoru included. Holding one anyway makes you weak, the blade learns nothing, and a whetstone won't raise a blade past what you could wield. You need:
after: A Supreme Grade katana can turn black for good. Fight with it for 2 hours (1 hour for a Kokuto blade) with your Armament Haki (level 4 or higher) switched on. Only real fighting counts: a hit on a foe in the last 5 seconds.

When it awakens, its blade becomes Black Blade Steel (8 damage, 2000 uses, the Black Blade trait) and it's fully mended. It keeps its tsuba, hilt, grade, level and enchantments, and the whole server hears about it.
> The katana's tooltip shows how many minutes it has so far.

chapters.title: Marine Disguise
text: Wear a full set of Arsenal armor (hat, coat, sash and boots) whose shells are all Navy materials, and Marines stop hunting you. How good the uniform is depends on its weakest shell:
- Recruit's uniform (Marine Standard Steel): hides a bounty up to 10M. Captains and CP agents see through it.
- Officer's uniform (Kairoseki or Pacifista Alloy): hides up to 100M. Vice Admirals, CP0, Pacifistas and Seraphim see through it.
- Admiral's uniform (Vegapunk Compound): hides up to 500M and fools every Marine.
# Blowing your cover
Hit a Marine and your cover is blown for a minute, even if you log out. Marines sent to hunt you give up after a minute too.
Named Marines like Garp and Smoker know who you are. No uniform fools them.

> Linings can be any material: a Kairoseki uniform with Driftwood linings is still a uniform. Navy linings make it a Regulation Uniform, which hides twice the bounty and draws suspicion half as fast (see Set Bonuses).

chapters.title: Suspicion
text: A uniform doesn't fool Marines forever. Marines who stand close and watch you get suspicious. They get suspicious faster:
- when there are several of them,
- when they're senior officers,
- when you hold a weapon or gun with a pirate-material blade, head or barrel (twice as fast),
- when your bounty is close to what the uniform can hide.
Stay too long and one of them calls you out: your cover is blown and the Marines who were watching attack. Walk away and they forget.
# Pirates see a Marine
Enemy pirates who spot you in a full Navy uniform drop whatever they're fighting and come for you, blown cover or not. Emperor crews still follow their Emperor's mood.
> In uniform, hold a weapon or gun with a Navy or common blade, head or barrel, like Marine Standard Steel or Cannon Bronze.

chapters.title: Finding Materials
text: # Crafted
- Driftwood: two sticks and a kelp.
- Cannon Bronze: copper melted with a cannonball, or with plain iron.
- Ship Iron and Treasure Gold: iron and gold ingots.
- Wano Tamahagane, Wapometal, Kairoseki and Adam Wood: the One Piece Mod's ingots and logs.
- Sea King Hide: its parts are made straight from the One Piece Mod's Sea King Scale.
# Vanilla materials
Plain Minecraft materials make parts too, at a crafting table, each with its own trait.
- Flint (Sparking), Stone from cobblestone (Crushing) and Copper ingots (Lightning Rod): cheap starter gear.
- Amethyst shards (Resonant), Emeralds (Trader's Charm) and Prismarine shards (Spined).
- Obsidian (Volcanic Glass) and Diamonds (Brilliant): as good as Wano steel and Kairoseki.
- Netherite ingots (Netherforged): the strongest, and its handles can't burn.
> A copper katana blade has an iron nugget at its foot, since three copper ingots make a Lightning Rod.
# From the islands
These come straight from the One Piece Mod's islands. Their parts are made at a crafting table.
- Dial Shell: Dial Shells from shell sand on beaches, in Skypiea, Jaya and the East Blue.
- Fishman Island Pearl: Sea Pearls from oyster gravel on the sea floor, in every ocean and around Fishman Island.
- Sabaody Resin (armor only): tap a Yarukiman tree on Sabaody with a Glass Bottle.
- Shandora Gold: Shandora Gold ore in Skypiea, Jaya, badlands and jungles.
- Kokuto Black Steel: Kokuto ore, rare and deep underground. A Kokuto katana awakens into a Black Blade in half the time.
- Dragon Scale (armor only): Punk Hazard's dragon.
# Taken in battle
- Sea King Bone: Sea Kings.
- Island Whale Leather: Island Whales.
- Pacifista Alloy: Pacifistas.
- Vegapunk Compound: Seraphim, and sometimes Vice Admirals.
- Marine Standard Steel: beaten Marines (officers more often), and chests in Marine bases and bunkers.
# Navy-issue weapons
Some Marines carry Arsenal katanas or flintlocks instead of their usual gear (Kairoseki blades for senior officers), and drop them now and then.
Vice Admirals, Commanders and famous Marines carry rarer gear still (see Navy Brass).
Bounty hunters carry forged pirate gear and drop it now and then (see Bounty Hunters).
> Black Blade Steel can't be crafted or looted. It's what a Supreme Grade katana's blade becomes when it awakens (see Meito).

chapters.title: Navy Brass
text: The Navy's top brass carry gear you can't forge anywhere else. Beat them yourself and they sometimes drop it. The crew a boss calls in to help never drops any of it.
# Vice Admirals and Commanders

- Vice Admirals: about 1 in 8 drop a Kairoseki or Pacifista Alloy part (a blade, jitte rod, barrel, hat crown or coat plates). About 1 in 50 drop their Vice Admiral's Blade instead, a Skillful Grade Kairoseki katana.
- Commanders and Captains: about 1 in 25 drop a Marine Steel or Kairoseki part.
# Famous Marines

Beat a famous Marine and they may drop their own named gear: 1 in 5 on Normal, 2 in 5 on Hard, 3 in 4 on Expert. Like the main mod's boss prizes, it only drops the first time you win at that difficulty, so you get one try per difficulty.
after: > Named gear is ordinary Arsenal gear with a name: it repairs, levels and takes whetstones like any other. Graded blades still refuse a wielder who isn't worthy (see Meito).

chapters.title: Bounty Hunters
text: Once your bounty reaches 100,000,000, bounty hunters with Devil Fruits come after you. They aren't Marines, so a Navy disguise won't fool them. They fight with forged pirate gear: a cutlass, boarding axe, kanabo, spear or katana, and some armor. The higher your bounty, the better their gear.
- Their weapon hits no harder than the sword they used to carry, but its type still counts: a kanabo knocks you far back and a spear reaches further.
- The best hunters sometimes carry Kairoseki. Every hit drains a Devil Fruit user's power for a few seconds, the same as Kairoseki in your own hands. So do Marine officers' Kairoseki blades.
- Beat a hunter and their weapon drops about 1 time in 10, each armor piece about 1 time in 20. It's worn from use, and its lore names who carried it.
after: > Check /bounty to see how many hunters come at a time at your bounty.
